notes: Premise verified: internal/proxy/admin_k8s.go:585-591 reads cluster_id as an optional query param and admin_ui.go:11375 omits it for the '전체 클러스터' view, so AnalyzeCapacity really is fed multi-cluster inventory+metrics. Name-only keys (nodes[it.Name], m.Namespace+"/"+m.ResourceName) therefore did cross-charge clusters. The fix is real.

Tests verified by mutation: I copied the tree to /tmp, reverted only the keying (nodeKey("",...) / podMetricKey("",...)) while keeping the new ClusterID fields, and all 5 new tests in internal/analyzer/capacity_cluster_test.go failed with the exact cross-cluster symptoms (packing collapsed to 1 row with Pods:3/ReqCPU:6000, prod/api flagged over_provisioned from dr's 250m sample, projection collapsed to one 8000m trend). They are not vacuous. Temp copy deleted; worktree left clean.

Key consistency confirmed: internal/collector/agent.go:114,130 and snapshot.go:60,132 stamp the same batch/snapshot ClusterID onto both inventory items and metric samples, and empty cluster_id is rejected (agent.go:88-89, snapshot.go:42-43). So inventory-side and metric-side keys cannot drift apart.

nodeKey is the pre-existing helper at internal/analyzer/node_monitoring.go:586 (clusterID+"\x00"+node), so the new keying matches how node_monitoring already keys nodes — consistent, and the \x00 separator avoids the ambiguity a plain "/" join would have.
go build ./..., go vet ./... and go test ./... all pass on HEAD.
Revert safety: change is confined to a read-only analysis path plus JSON field additions marked omitempty. No schema migration, no writes, no external state. Trivially revertible.

Minor (not blocking): admin_ui.go:11204 k8sNodePacking falls back to matching a row with empty cluster_id against any node name. That path is currently unreachable (cluster_id is always populated) and degrades to the old behaviour if it ever fires, so it is a safe fallback rather than a bug.

Minor (not blocking): admin_ui.go:15324 nodeVisual renders only n.node, so two same-named nodes from different clusters appear as identical tiles there, unlike the packing/GPU tables at 15307/15313 which now carry a cluster_id sub-label. Cosmetic inconsistency in the same screen.

Minor (not blocking): admin_ui.go:11433 still slices node_packing to the first 20 rows. With one row per cluster-node the fleet view now produces more rows, and the new sort is alphabetical by cluster then node, so truncation drops later clusters rather than the least-loaded nodes. Ordering was random before, so this is not a regression, but sorting by cpu_request_pct would suit a top-20 list better.
Scope is tight: no refactors, dependency bumps or unrelated formatting; every UI edit is a consumer of the fields this fix adds.
